tooltip.dt.m1_helmet.style: "In 1941, this 'pot' debuted and accompanied the U.S. Army for four decades, from Pacific islands to Southeast Asian jungles, becoming the most familiar sight atop a generation of soldiers."
tooltip.dt.mk2_helmet.style: "In 1915, the 'flying saucer' forged by John Brodie was discovered by the 'Tommy' soldiers; soon, disc-shaped steel helmets appeared in groups along the coasts of both World Wars."
tooltip.dt.m35_helmet.style: "In 1935, the gray boy was born: it kept the M16's familiar outline, but the doctrine behind it was already marching in the opposite direction, toward a very different and ultimately ruinous war."
tooltip.dt.m35_helmet_2.style: "In 1936, M35s bearing the Blue Sky with a White Sun came to China from Germany—the first large-scale issue anywhere, and for the next eight years, a mirror of that generation’s soldiers in the anti-fascist war."
tooltip.dt.ssh40_helmet.style: "In 1940, the Soviets issued a riveted half-sphere: six bolts, three pads, and a million stories from Stalingrad to the Reichstag."
tooltip.dt.j90type_helmet.style: "In 1930,Japan's \"steel bowl\" was born—too thin for bullets, too cold for winter, too shiny for snipers."
info.dt.t26:
The T-26 was a Soviet light tank of the 1930s, developed from the British Vickers 6-Ton. In 1930 the USSR purchased 15 Vickers prototypes, reverse-engineered and localized them, and adopted the T-26 for mass production in 1931.
Between 1938 and 1942, under the Sino-Soviet Non-Aggression Pact, the USSR supplied China with about 82 T-26 tanks, mainly Mod. 1933 vehicles.
